 Do you have a Thanksgiving dinner specialty? With my limited cooking skills, I whip up the easiest classic to make from scratch: cranberry sauce . I always get compliments, but maybe my relatives are just taking pity.
 Growth and harvest are themes of today’s newsletter. Here’s what we have:
 Farmers’ market tips for the Thanksgiving season.
 A look at a Walker Art Center exhibition that includes both fresh flowers and rammed earth.
 A tally of big wins by local teams.
 Five must-reads and the weekend weather forecast.
 Why a nine-foot bear has taken up residence at Allianz Field.
 Sign up here to get this newsletter delivered to your inbox or share this link with a friend who might like to join us. 
 This week at the farmer’s market
 Image Credit... Bobbi Lin for The New York Times By Talya Minsberg 
 We’re nearing mid-November, and many of us are planning our Thanksgiving menu. To get some ideas on what’s fresh, I chatted with Lindsay Stauner, the assistant director of the St. Paul Growers’ Association. “I get a lot of questions about cranberries this time of year,” she said, adding that yes, they are in season, and yes, it’s a good time to buy them.
 Sam Sifton has a great New York Times Cooking recipe for a simple cranberry sauce . It freezes well if you decide to make it before the holiday.
 There are also a lot of hearty winter vegetables in season, Stauner said, including brussels sprouts, beets and cabbage.
 Here are recipes for roasted brussels sprouts with garlic and brussels sprouts buried in cream . If you are looking to make a cozy meal out of your farmers’ market trip, try this recipe for cabbage, potato and leek soup .
